notes: Actual results for calendar year 2024, as the town reported them in its Municipal Financial Report to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Oconto County.
Wisconsin towns govern the rural areas outside cities and villages; cities and villages are separate from the town around them.
Governmental funds are reported by function. Water, sewer, electric and other utility and enterprise funds are reported only as total revenues and expenses, counted as utility charges and utilities.
Other financing sources ($45,261: borrowing, transfers and refunding) and uses ($0) are left out.
General government, conservation and development, and other spending count as overhead.
Debt is general obligation debt outstanding at year end, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Wisconsin local candidates file campaign finance reports with their municipal clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 1 license-plate camera is mapped inside Town of Underhill's borders in OpenStreetMap (1 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Wisconsin yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 1 Flock Safety license-plate camera is mapped inside Town of Underhill's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
